meta.title: Paid on the Pass
meta.theme: how a grant paid on examination passes changed what schools taught, and which of the two practices it produced survived the grant

format.format_verified: 2026-09: five sentences, TITA, +3 with no negative marking, consistent in released papers 2016 to 2025; re-verify against each new official paper

traps.description: The outlier is a concrete scene from exactly the day the story turns on, the inspector's visit, and the story has just said that children were kept away on that day, so the scene appears to be the illustration the narrative was building to. The decoy is the short sentence about which of the two practices stopped, whose bare arithmetic reads like a note rather than a stage of a story.

meta.learning_objective: ask what claim an example is serving before admitting it, and notice when a vivid instance illustrates something the paragraph never asserts

quality.adversarial_review: The live rival is the short sentence saying that one of the two practices stopped within a year and the other did not: it is the barest sentence in the set, it reads like a note rather than an event, and a reader assembling a story may treat it as arithmetic rather than narrative. It stays because the closing sentence distinguishes what outlasted the grant from the practice that ended with it, and only this sentence says that one of them ended; remove it and the ending sorts two practices the story has never sorted. The scene in the hired hall is the visitor. It belongs to the inspection day the story has just mentioned, and it is vivid enough to look like the illustration the narrative was heading for, but the story's claims are about what a payment rule did to teaching, and no claim in it concerns the conditions children were examined in.

source.usage_note: Original composition in CAT register for CAT OS. General account of grants paid on examination results in elementary schooling; no specific text adapted. Personal study only.

meta.reviewer_notes: The example is placed on the very day the narrative turns on, so topic matching and even time matching approve it. What excludes it is that the story asserts nothing it could illustrate, and that the three joints of the core, the rule, the second of those two practices and the practice that ended with the grant, each lose their antecedent when a neighbour is removed.

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: In one district the examination was held in a hired hall, and children who had walked four miles in the rain were heard in wet clothes at the far end of a room with a single stove.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: Masters answered the rule as anyone would, by teaching the list and by keeping the weakest children at home, scrubbed and idle, on the day the inspector came.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: A grant paid on the number of pupils who passed an inspector's annual examination made a school's income depend on a list of six separately testable things.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: When the grant was detached from the examination the second of those two practices stopped within a year and the first did not.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: What outlasted the arithmetic was not the practice that ended with it but the shape of the lesson it had required, and a syllabus of separately examinable items went on being taught by masters who had never been paid by it.

builder.prompt: Build the four-sentence story of a grant paid on examination passes, from the rule to what was still being taught after the money had gone. The sentence that is vivid about the same day and illustrates no claim the story makes is your answer.

explanation.spine_note: The core tells one story in four stages. A grant paid on passes makes a school's income depend on a list of separately testable things; masters answer the rule in two ways, by teaching the list and by keeping the weakest children away on inspection day; when the grant is detached from the examination the second of those practices stops at once and the first does not; and what outlasts the money is the shape of the lesson the money required. Rule, response, withdrawal, residue.

core_roles.label: C
core_roles.why_here: It supplies the payment rule the entire story is a consequence of, and the list of separately testable things that the last sentence finds still in use.

core_roles.label: B
core_roles.why_here: 'The rule' names the grant just described, and this is the stage at which it reaches the classroom, in the two practices the story later has to sort.

core_roles.label: D
core_roles.why_here: 'The second of those two practices' counts the pair just given, and this stage removes the money and reports which response depended on it.

core_roles.label: E
core_roles.why_here: It separates the practice that ended from the shape that did not, which is the point the whole sequence was assembled to reach.

links.explanation: 'The rule' points at the grant just described, which makes the masters' conduct a response rather than a coincidence.
'The second of those two practices' is a count with exactly one antecedent, the pair of responses the previous sentence lists.
'The practice that ended with it' names the one the previous sentence says stopped, so the closing contrast cannot be drawn without it.

explanation.violation_named: The odd sentence is an example, and an example has to be an example of something. The four core sentences claim that a payment rule shaped what was taught and that one of its effects outlived it. The scene in the hired hall shows the conditions children were examined in, and the paragraph makes no claim about conditions at all.
explanation.why_it_breaks: No sentence before it needs illustrating by it and no sentence after it uses it. The story's two practices are teaching to the list and keeping weak children away; a cold hall and wet clothes belong to neither. The closing sentence sorts what survived from what did not, and a scene has nothing to contribute to a sorting. It also stops the clock: the narrative moves from rule to response to withdrawal to residue, and the scene occupies a day that has no place in that sequence.
explanation.trap_exposed: The camouflage is placement in time. The story has just said that children were kept at home on the day the inspector came, so a scene set on that very day looks like the illustration the paragraph was building to, and it shares the period, the inspector and the children. The test is whether the paragraph asserts anything the scene could show, and it asserts only things about payment and teaching. The decoy is the short sentence about which practice stopped, whose flat arithmetic reads like an aside, though it is the only sentence that ends one of the two practices and the only antecedent the ending has.

exclusion_analysis.label: C
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It is about money and administration rather than about a school, so a reader who has decided the paragraph is about teaching may treat it as preliminary.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without it 'the rule' points at nothing, and a story about masters responding to an incentive never says what the incentive was.

exclusion_analysis.label: B
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It packs two unlike responses into one clause, and the second of them is discreditable enough to read like an aside about conduct.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without it the count in the next sentence has nothing to count, and the shape of the lesson that survives has never been shown being adopted.

exclusion_analysis.label: D
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It is the shortest sentence in the set and the only one with no detail in it, which can make it look like a bridge the story could do without.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without it the money is never withdrawn, and the closing distinction between the practice that ended and the shape that lasted has nothing to rest on.

exclusion_analysis.label: E
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It is the longest sentence and reaches past the story's own period, so it can look like a summary appended after the narrative has finished.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without it the story describes a rule, a response and a withdrawal and never says what any of it left behind, which is the only thing it was heading for.

explanation.detection_habit: Before you admit an example, name the sentence it is an example of. A vivid instance on the right day, in the right period, among the right people can still be illustrating a claim the paragraph never made.

mentor.challenge: One of these sentences puts you in the room on the day everything turns on. Ask which claim in the paragraph that room is evidence for before you let it stay.
mentor.takeaway: An example without a claim is scenery. Find the sentence it serves, or find it a door.
